newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Dec 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Dec 27.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on December 27:

WASHINGTON - The D.C. Financial Control Board plans to slash at least 1,000 jobs and $85 million in expenditures from the District's budget to prevent overspending and assure federal officials that the funds are being managed carefully.
WASHINGTON - The pace was sluggish in many area offices Thursday as thousands of workers took advantage of a midweek Christmas to craft a five-day weekend.
TOKYO - More than 150,000 workers in South Korea went on strike Thursday and as many as 1.2 million more plan to join them for a one-day work stoppage Friday to protest labour laws.

WASHINGTON - A Thai businesswoman who is a major donor to the Democratic Party brought five business associates to a White House coffee meeting with President Clinton the same day she and a relative gave $135,000 to the Democratic National Committee.

WASHINGTON - Two years ago, a group called Sons of Confederate Veterans asked the Maryland state government to issue special automobile license plates for members of the non-profit organisation, but the design of the approved tag has touched a nerve among some African Americans.

WASHINGTON - After predicting a holiday season in which they would jingle all the way to the bank, retailers have begun reporting sales figures that outpace last year's performance, but fall below earlier hopes.
